plan: Keep the deep-copied data dict as the single source of truth: a recursive composite tree where sections/groups have 'items' and notes/references are leaves; the workspace root's item list is just the top container level.

total_word_count(): recursive aggregation — notes strip [[?...]] markers (replaced with a space so adjacent words don't merge) then count \b\w+\b runs; references contribute their declared word_count; containers sum children.
unresolved_markers(): recursive collection into a set (marker identifiers from note text via regex capture, plus references' unresolved lists), returned sorted lexicographically.
outline(): deterministic pre-order depth-first traversal; workspace title first, then each item as two-spaces-per-level indentation + '<kind>: <title>', top-level items at level 1.

move(): full pre-validation (string ids, item exists, destination is 'workspace' or an existing section/group, destination id not in the moved item's subtree id-set covering self/cycle cases, explicit index within 0..len(destination)) before any mutation, then pop from the old parent list and append/insert — so any ValueError leaves state untouched and success preserves the whole subtree.
to_data(): deepcopy on construction and export to isolate the workspace from callers.
mechanisms: recursive part-whole composite over a dict tree
uniform recursive aggregation for word counts
recursive set-collection with sorted output for unresolved markers
containment invariant via subtree id-set check (no self-containment or cycles)
defensive deep copying at construction and export
